events.title: The Pirate Bay BitTorrent tracker founded
events.summary: Gottfrid Svartholm, Fredrik Neij, and Peter Sunde launched The Pirate Bay on September 15, 2003 — a BitTorrent indexer that became the world's most famous piracy site.
events.about: TPB hosted .torrent files and magnet links for movies, games, and software — the successor to Napster and warez FTP topsites in the BitTorrent era. Raids, domain seizures, and prison sentences for its founders made it a symbol of copyright resistance; developers studied its resilience tactics for censorship-resistant systems (and rights holders studied takedown law).

narrative.whyChosen: The Pirate Bay was the flagship of post-Napster BitTorrent piracy.
narrative.whyImportant: It kept public attention on P2P enforcement and inspired decentralization experiments.
narrative.problemSolved: This was illicit distribution — it showed how resilient indexing could be against legal pressure.

events.title: Xcode 1.0 released
events.summary: Apple shipped Xcode 1.0 on September 28, 2003 — integrating Project Builder into a modern Mac IDE ahead of Mac OS X Panther.
events.about: Xcode became the mandatory toolchain for iOS and macOS development — Interface Builder, Instruments, lldb, and Swift support all live here. Every App Store binary is built with Xcode's compiler and signing pipeline.

narrative.whyChosen: Xcode is Apple's primary IDE for native platform development.
narrative.whyImportant: It unified Mac (and later iPhone) tooling under one environment.
narrative.problemSolved: Mac developers used fragmented Project Builder and external debuggers.
